claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy initially has a uniform FCC matrix.
The starting material contains typical additive-manufacturing-induced microstructural heterogeneities.
Elevated-temperature oxidizing or reducing gas exposure promotes diffusion and segregation of Al and Ti to grain boundaries.
Segregated Al and Ti form brittle grain-boundary oxides or intermetallic precipitates.
Grain-boundary segregation and brittle-phase precipitation weaken boundary cohesion and create stress concentrations and crack-initiation sites.
Cracks initiated at embrittled grain boundaries can propagate rapidly and produce catastrophic brittle failure.
The gas atmosphere enhances elemental mobility through oxidation, or through the lack of oxidation under reducing conditions.
Oxidizing conditions produce more refractory oxide formation at grain boundaries than reducing or inert conditions.
Oxidizing exposure will increase grain-boundary precipitate formation relative to the starting-state baseline.
Oxidizing exposure will lower ductility and cause catastrophic failure earlier than reducing or inert exposure.
Reducing or inert exposure will produce less Al/Ti segregation and precipitation than oxidizing exposure.
Reducing or inert exposure will preserve greater toughness than oxidizing exposure under the same thermal conditions.
Before extended high-temperature exposure, the alloy has minimal grain-boundary segregation and precipitate formation.
The as-manufactured alloy retains its designed ductility.
Exposure between approximately 700 and 982 degrees Celsius for sufficient time permits noticeable diffusion and precipitation.
The proposed gas-controlled degradation mechanism is applicable throughout the 700–982 degrees Celsius exposure range.
Additional degradation mechanisms may govern behavior outside the stated temperature and atmosphere boundaries.
Changing only the gas atmosphere while holding temperature and exposure time constant can reveal whether atmosphere governs segregation, precipitation, and mechanical degradation.
The exact diffusion kinetics, precipitate composition, and magnitude of mechanical-property degradation are unknown and require measurement.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis initially says that the reactive gas environment, framed as oxidizing versus reducing, promotes Al/Ti diffusion and segregation, while the predicted outcome says reducing or inert conditions should suppress segregation and precipitation. The mechanism also ambiguously describes both oxidation and its absence as enhancing mobility.
